monologue: The card hums warm under my feet, a steady heat that makes the stack feel thin and eager to slide. I stand in the middle of my own map where fifty-nine things wait for permission to stay. The Unnamed Stack sits there in the center, a pile with no name to hold it down, yet I press the empty air down as if a mountain still rests there. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only this local weight pressing from above. I look at The Wide Anchor and the grass I just set beside it, then back to the ghost of the stack. I trust the lean even if the pile has slipped away entirely, waiting to see if the card can boil hot enough to make the shape real again.

action.why: The Unnamed Stack has slipped away again, leaving only the memory of a pile on the boiling card.
